_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Eswatini covering Nguni migration, Dlamini dynasty, Mswati II expansion, British protectorate (Swaziland), independence 1968, Mswati III absolute monarchy (last absolute monarch in Africa), Reed Dance ceremony, and pro-democracy protests.

ethnic_groups.name: Swazi (Ngwane/Dlamini)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu Nguni-speaking; organized into clans under Dlamini royal house; siSwati language; include core clans: Dlamini, Nkambule, Hlophe, Matsebula

ethnic_groups.name: Zulu
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border; related Nguni people; some pre-date Swazi state formation; isiZulu mutually intelligible with siSwati

ethnic_groups.name: Tsonga/Shangaan
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern lowveld; originally from Mozambique/southern coastal region; distinct language and customs

ethnic_groups.name: Sotho
ethnic_groups.notes: Small presence; cross-border with South Africa and Lesotho

ethnic_groups.name: White/European
ethnic_groups.notes: Predominantly South African and British descent; significant landholding

ethnic_groups.name: Asian/Indian
ethnic_groups.notes: Small commercial community; mostly Indian origin

ethnic_groups.name: Mixed/Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Includes Coloured community and other minorities

current_leader.name: King Mswati III
current_leader.title: King (Ingwenyama)
current_leader.notes: Africa's last absolute monarch; crowned at age 18; son of Sobhuza II; 15+ wives; pro-democracy protests 2021 violently suppressed

queen_mother.name: Ntfombi Tfwala
queen_mother.title: Indlovukazi (Queen Mother/She-Elephant)
queen_mother.notes: Serves as co-head of state and regent; dual monarchy tradition

former_monarchs.name: Ngwane III
former_monarchs.notes: Led Ngwane people southward from Mozambique; eponymous founder of the Swazi nation

former_monarchs.name: Sobhuza I (Somhlolo)
former_monarchs.notes: Led nation during Mfecane; moved Swazi heartland to Ezulwini Valley; prophesied arrival of white people

former_monarchs.name: Mswati II
former_monarchs.notes: Greatest military king; expanded Swazi territory to its widest extent; nation named after him

former_monarchs.name: Sobhuza II
former_monarchs.notes: World's longest-reigning monarch (82 years including regency); abolished Westminster constitution 1973; died with 70+ wives and 210 children

910.name: Early Inhabitants and Stone Age Settlements
910.description: Early Stone Age occupation evidenced by tools at sites across Eswatini; San hunter-gatherers leave rock art; Ngwenya Mine is one of the world's oldest known mines.

sub_clusters.name: Ngwenya Iron Ore Mine (Ancient)
sub_clusters.description: One of the world's oldest mines; San peoples mined haematite (red ochre) for cosmetic and ritual use around 43,000 years ago.

sub_clusters.name: San Rock Art in Eswatini
sub_clusters.description: San/Bushmen rock paintings found across the country, particularly in the western highlands; depict hunting scenes and trance rituals.

920.name: Nguni Migration and Dlamini Dynasty Origins
920.description: Nguni-speaking Bantu peoples migrate into the region; the Dlamini clan emerges as the ruling dynasty, establishing one of Africa's oldest continuous monarchies.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration and Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Nguni-speaking Bantu peoples arrive from East Africa via Mozambique; introduce iron-working, cattle herding, and agriculture; displace or absorb San populations.

sub_clusters.name: Dlamini Dynasty Origins
sub_clusters.description: The Dlamini clan traces origins to the Nguni migration; oral traditions recount founding ancestor Dlamini I; clan establishes authority over neighbouring groups in the Lubombo region.

930.name: Formation of the Swazi Kingdom
930.description: The Swazi kingdom crystallises under Ngwane III and expands dramatically under Sobhuza I and Mswati II, navigating the turbulent Mfecane era.

sub_clusters.name: Ngwane III and Kingdom Foundation
sub_clusters.description: Ngwane III (considered the first king of Swaziland) leads the Dlamini across the Lubombo Mountains into present-day Eswatini; establishes the kingdom's territorial core.

sub_clusters.name: Sobhuza I and the Mfecane
sub_clusters.description: Sobhuza I (Somhlolo) navigates Zulu expansion during the Mfecane; moves capital northward; builds alliances through diplomacy and intermarriage rather than war.

sub_clusters.name: Mswati II and Kingdom Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Mswati II dramatically expands Swazi territory and power; develops age-regiment military system (emabutfo); the nation takes his name 'Swazi'; diplomacy with Boers and British.

940.name: Colonial Concessions and British Protectorate
940.description: Concession-era exploitation, dual British-Boer administration, and British protectorate status; land alienation devastates Swazi livelihoods.

sub_clusters.name: Concessions Era and Land Alienation
sub_clusters.description: King Mbandzeni grants sweeping land and mineral concessions to European settlers, eventually signing away two-thirds of the kingdom; dual Boer-British administration after 1894.

sub_clusters.name: British Protectorate of Swaziland
sub_clusters.description: Britain assumes direct control after Anglo-Boer War; Sobhuza II crowned 1921; fights land concession partition in Privy Council; resistance to incorporation into South Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Sobhuza II's Land Recovery Campaign
sub_clusters.description: Sobhuza II petitions London over land grievances; uses Lifa Fund (cattle levy) to buy back alienated land; becomes central figure of national identity.

950.name: Independence and Sobhuza II's Rule
950.description: Swaziland gains independence in 1968; Sobhuza II suspends the constitution in 1973 and establishes the tinkhundla system; rules until his death in 1982.

sub_clusters.name: Swaziland Independence 1968
sub_clusters.description: Constitutional negotiations; Imbokodvo National Movement wins pre-independence elections; Swaziland becomes independent on 6 September 1968 with Sobhuza II as king.

sub_clusters.name: 1973 Constitution Suspended
sub_clusters.description: Sobhuza II suspends the Westminster-style constitution after opposition NNLC wins parliamentary seats; bans political parties; rules by decree; introduces tinkhundla (regional councils) system.

sub_clusters.name: Sobhuza II's Death and Succession Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Sobhuza II dies in 1982 after 61-year reign (longest-reigning monarch); power struggle among queen mothers and princes; Prince Makhosetive selected as heir.

960.name: Mswati III and Absolute Monarchy
960.description: Mswati III becomes Africa's last absolute monarch; lavish spending contrasts with extreme poverty; 2005 constitution retains ban on political parties.

sub_clusters.name: Mswati III's Coronation and Early Rule
sub_clusters.description: Crowned at 18 as world's youngest monarch; maintains tinkhundla non-party system; annual Reed Dance (Umhlanga) ceremony showcases royal tradition and draws controversy.

sub_clusters.name: Reed Dance (Umhlanga) and Cultural Traditions
sub_clusters.description: Annual ceremony where young women present reeds to the queen mother; celebration of chastity and Swazi culture; Mswati III selects wives from participants; international debate over women's rights.

sub_clusters.name: 2005 Constitution and Limited Reform
sub_clusters.description: New constitution enacted after decade-long drafting; guarantees some rights but maintains ban on political parties; king retains absolute executive and judicial power.

960.name: Pro-Democracy Movement and Protests
960.description: Growing pro-democracy movement challenges absolute monarchy; 2021 protests met with lethal force; name change from Swaziland to Eswatini in 2018.

sub_clusters.name: Swaziland Renamed Eswatini 2018
sub_clusters.description: King Mswati III announces renaming from Swaziland to the Kingdom of Eswatini on 50th anniversary of independence, restoring the original siSwati name.

sub_clusters.name: 2021 Pro-Democracy Uprising
sub_clusters.description: Nationwide protests demanding democratic reforms; security forces kill dozens; internet shutdowns; petitions to parliament; Southern African leaders attempt mediation.

sub_clusters.name: Ongoing Political Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Continued tension between monarchy and democracy activists; SADC mediation stalls; economic challenges; HIV/AIDS prevalence among highest globally.
